A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Event2Vec by the same authors. All 19 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison. Relocated and reformatted material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original classification results on three datasets, throughput and latency measurements, embedding ablations, event-count experiments and learned-representation visualizations.

after.justification: V4 retains original classification experiments and reports additional resolution, transfer, clustering, attention-type and parameter-sharing evaluations in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: V4 introduces GPU batched K-Means++ initialization and incremental distance updates (Algorithm 1). For clustered events, fusion changes from rho*spatial + temporal in v3 Equation 7 to (log(rho)+1)*(spatial+temporal) in v4 Equation 6. Appendix A.5 also revises the described pretraining masking to include consecutive spans with geometrically distributed lengths averaging 10 tokens.

E1.justification: The same three classification datasets remain: DVS Gesture, ASL-DVS and DVS-Lip. V4 adds degraded-input coverage through simulated DVS Gesture spatial resolutions ranging from 128×128 down to 1×1 (Figure 3), without adding another dataset or application domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Max-Former to the DVS Gesture accuracy comparison. The DVS Gesture efficiency comparison replaces FARSE-CNN, AEGNN, SNN/PLIF-Net and Sparse GRU with Max-Former; v4 Table 2 also evaluates dataset-specific comparators on ASL-DVS and DVS-Lip. New Table 4 compares clustering against Scikit-learn and Faiss configurations.

E3.justification: V3's separate whole-training-set preprocessing benchmark and DVS Gesture model timings are replaced by per-stream preprocessing, forward and total latency plus GPU memory measurements across three datasets. V4 specifies a memory-limited throughput batch-selection rule and adds resolution-perturbation and frozen five-layer linear-probing protocols. Appendix A.9 also adds DVS-Lip temporal chunk dropping and revises its stated flip probability.

E4.justification: V4 adds spatial-resolution robustness, cross-dataset linear probing, clustering speed–accuracy comparisons, FoX-versus-GLA ablations and shared-versus-unshared bidirectional attention analyses. Existing embedding ablations and visualizations remain. The DVS Gesture event-count study moves to Appendix A.7, while the corresponding ASL-DVS quantitative panel is omitted and replaced by a statement that trends are similar.

E5.justification: Both versions retain mean±standard-deviation reporting and 10 test-set runs for random-sampling experiments. V4 removes the statement fixing Python, NumPy and PyTorch seeds to zero and the preprocessing benchmark's explicit two warm-up/eight measurement-run disclosure. These are losses of statistical documentation, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Table 1's DVS-Lip cluster accuracy changes from 75.14% to 75.88% alongside revised clustering and training, while the three random-event accuracy entries remain unchanged. Tan et al.'s entry changes from 60.3%/72.1 MB to 72.1%/241.20 MB; the spiking baseline's size changes from 58.6 to 223.63 MB. V4 adds substantial efficiency, robustness and ablation results, including linear-probing accuracies of 86.94±1.21% and 69.83±7.66%.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix A.2's fixed-state recurrence formulation is replaced in v4 Appendix A.4 by Q/K/V attention equations with explicit reversal of backward outputs before fusion. V4 distinguishes FoX from linear attention and removes the earlier O(L) scaling interpretation. These are localized formal corrections; the spatial Taylor-expansion argument remains substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central event2vec and neighborhood-embedding contributions remain. V4 extends the advertised benefits to low latency and low spatial resolutions and claims the highest compared DVS-Lip accuracy. Its abstract and introduction emphasize first reconciling sparse events with GPU-efficient Transformers, while the earlier NLP/LLM integration perspective remains in the conclusion.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands mechanism and applicability interpretations. It links temporal convolutions to smoothing and temporal preconditioning, interprets 1×1-resolution performance as evidence for temporal encoding, and interprets probing results as transferable representations. New appendix discussions attribute GLA's DVS-Lip deficit to memory decay and unshared attention's lower accuracy to overfitting. Existing random-sampling limitations and misplaced-attention examples remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds clustering normalization, allocation and GPU implementation instructions in Algorithm 1 and comparator augmentation documentation in Table 8. However, it removes explicit dataset-split descriptions, benchmark batch/worker/library details and special small-event augmentation instructions. The code URL remains, but the reproducibility statement and explicit promise of trained models and logs disappear; actual repository availability cannot be determined from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The dense-versus-irregular representation literature review remains largely intact. V4 adds focused references for K-Means++, Max-Former, linear probing, residual learning and GLA, while removing several sources associated with the old benchmarking implementations, including SpikingJelly, Tonic and Haste. Its novelty positioning places greater emphasis on combining sparse representations with GPU-efficient dense models.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution framing, temporal rationale, network description and efficiency discussion undergo substantial rewriting. Existing appendix material is extensively reorganized, and architecture and event-count discussion move out of the main text. A generic Impact Statement is added. V4 also introduces the erroneous running header 'Submission and Formatting Instructions for ICML 2026'.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column main text and extensively restructures performance tables. V3 Figure 2 is redrawn and moved to the appendix as v4 Figure 6, with normalization, pooling and revised fusion shown. The event-count chart is redrawn as a DVS Gesture-only appendix figure. New resolution, algorithm and ablation displays accompany rearranged retained visualizations.

improvement.justification: V4 improves support for the paper's efficiency and representation claims through separated end-to-end latency and memory measurements, explicit clustering procedures and comparisons, and new robustness, transfer and component analyses. Appendix A.4 also repairs the characterization of FoX. However, removing split, seed and timing-procedure documentation reduces reproducibility, and replacing the broader DVS Gesture efficiency comparator panel narrows that comparison. The added evidence provides a net quality benefit, moderated by these reporting losses.
